append.text: **Ps 59:3, 59:12 *repulísti nos* → *vós nos repelistes … que nos repelistes*** — the row applied twice in one psalm. **The blind reader of Ps 59 did not know *repelistes* either — the second psalm to report it (after 42).** *rejeitastes* (reprobáre's), *desamparastes* (MS1932) options.

**Ps 59:4 *sana contritiónes ejus* → *curai as suas fraturas*** (συντρίμματα, the breakings of the earth, healed); as the row foresaw, *ruína* cannot be healed. *brechas* (DRB), *chagas* (MS1932) options. 146:3 *álligat contritiónes eórum* should weigh *fraturas*. No reader objected.

**Ps 59:8 *Deus locútus est in sancto suo* → *Deus falou no seu santo*** (v2): the Latinist and the stylist both said *no seu lugar santo* settles as a place what the bare neuter leaves open (place / holiness / holy one); the stylist's word-for-word *no seu santo* taken and passed the gate. *no seu lugar santo*, *no seu santuário* options. The row stands where *in sancto* is plainly a place (19:3, 21:4).

**Ps 59:6 *ut fúgiant a fácie arcus* → *para que fujam da face do arco*** (v2, the stylist: *de diante do* (MS1932) tripped and thinned the image); the row's *da face de* after a verb of flight. Passed the gate. The colon is sung alone in the office of St Emygdius (Urbis/08-09).

**Ps 59:14 *In Deo faciémus virtútem* → *Em Deus agiremos com poder*** (= 117:16's build; 107:14 should copy). No reader remarked. In the same psalm 59:12's plural *virtútes* is *forças* (D43) — the accepted cost.

**Ps 59:11 *Quis dedúcet me … quis dedúcet me* → *Quem me guiará … quem me guiará*** (the repetition kept where the Greek varies; MS1932 *conduzirá* option); the stylist's best line. 107:11 should copy.
Ps 59:11 *in civitátem munítam* → *à cidade fortificada* — applied; no remark. 107:11 copies.
Ps 59:12b copies 43:10b (with the question mark); the blind reader heard strength first, troops second — the Latin's range.
Ps 59:14 *tribulántes nos* → *os que nos atribulam* — unknown to the blind reader again (the fifth psalm); kept, beside *tribulação* in 59:13.
Ps 59:14 *ad níhilum dedúcet* → *reduzirá a nada* — applied; heard as 'destroy' first.
Ps 59:8 *convállem tabernaculórum* → *o vale das tendas* (the Latin translates the place name; MS1932 *vale dos Tabernáculos* option).

**Ps 59:13 *Da nobis auxílium de tribulatióne* → *Dai-nos auxílio na tribulação*** (MS1932): draft 1 *contra a tribulação* (31:7's build) was marked by the v1 Latinist as leaning to the Hebrew; the v2 gate asked for *contra* back. The runs contradict each other; *na* held, *contra* the option — for Gustavo. The colon is a Matins antiphon (*Da nobis * Dómine auxílium de tribulatióne*, Psalmi matutinum). 107:13 copies.
Ps 59:10 *mihi alienígenæ súbditi sunt* → *a mim estão sujeitos os estrangeiros* (the state; *foram sujeitos* option). 107:10 differs (*amíci facti sunt*).
Ps 59:7 *salvum fac déxtera tua* (no object) → *salvai com a vossa direita* — the Latin's missing object not supplied (*salvai-me* DRB, *salvai-nos* MS1932 options); no reader remarked. 107:7 copies.

terms: | compúnctio (*vinum compunctiónis*) | compunção (*destes-nos a beber vinho de compunção*) | open | Ps 59:5 only (grep the psalter before ruling); the noun of 4:5 *compungi-vos*; the Greek κατάνυξις is stupor. The blind reader did not know *compunção*; MS1932 *amargura*, *aturdimento* (the Greek's sense) options. |

| olla / lebes (Moab's pot) | panela (*Moab é a panela da minha esperança*) | open | Ps 59:9b *olla*; 107:10 has *lebes* for the same Greek (λέβης) — by D15's test it may copy *panela*, or take *caldeirão* to show the Latin's variation. The stylist kept *panela* for the image; the blind reader heard the slang 'clique' and missed the contempt. *caldeira*, *vaso* (MS1932) options. |
| calceaméntum | calçado (*estenderei o meu calçado*) | open | Ps 59:10 = 107:10. MS1932; *sandália* option. The blind reader found the gesture obscure (the Latin's image). |
| alienígenæ | estrangeiros | open | Ps 59:10 = 107:10 (ἀλλόφυλοι); kept apart from *aliénus → estranho* (17:46 *filhos estranhos*). 82:8, 86:4 (grep) should follow. |

| partíri / divídere (land) | repartir (*e repartirei Siquém*) | open | Ps 59:8 *partíbor*; 107:8 *dívidam* is the same Greek (διαμεριῶ) and should copy; = 21:18 *repartiram*. Rule 3 applies only at the imperative (*reparti*). |
| significátio | sinal (*Destes aos que vos temem um sinal*) | open | Ps 59:6 (σημείωσις); the blind reader heard signal, banner and miracle — the Latin's range. |
formulas: | *Da nobis, (Dómine,) auxílium de tribulatióne: quia vana salus hóminis* (59:13 = 107:13; the Matins antiphon *Da nobis * Dómine auxílium de tribulatióne*, Psalmi matutinum; versicles of 08-SanteDultim, aliquibus locis — grep) | *Dai-nos auxílio na tribulação: * porque é vã a salvação do homem* | open — Ps 59; *contra a tribulação* the option (the Latinist's two runs disagree); 107:13 copies |

| Ps 59:7–14 ↔ Ps 107:6b–14 (the doublet's second half) | Ps 107 copies Ps 59 wherever the Latin is identical: *para que sejam livrados os vossos amados*; *salvai com a vossa direita, e escutai-me*; *Deus falou no seu santo*; *Meu é Galaad, e meu é Manassés*; *Judá é o meu rei*; *Sobre a Idumeia estenderei o meu calçado*; 59:11 whole; *Não sereis vós, Deus, que nos repelistes?*; 59:13 whole; *Em Deus agiremos com poder: * e ele mesmo reduzirá a nada …* | open — Ps 59; Ps 107 decides only where its Latin differs (*exsultábo, dívidam, dimétiar, suscéptio, lebes, amíci facti sunt, exíbis, inimícos nostros*) |
